small_guidance:
- The conv (Conv3d with B=1024, C=16, output 13×29×29) almost certainly dominates runtime at ~8.2ms; further tuning of `BLOCK_S` / `num_warps` in the post-conv kernel will not close the gap. If staying small, try collapsing the post-conv kernel to one program per batch (combine all groups) and using `tl.sum(..., axis=1)` over the full channel block, so launch overhead drops from `B*num_groups=4096` programs to `B=1024`.
- Add autotune configs at `BLOCK_S=512` with `num_warps=2` since per-group S=10933 is only ~11 chunks at 1024 — overhead-bound rather than bandwidth-bound; smaller tiles may overlap better.
- Pre-fold the conv bias into the kernel epilogue if not already, and ensure `x_flat` is created without an extra `.contiguous()` copy when conv output is already contiguous.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.Conv3d` with a custom Triton im2col-style GEMM kernel: with IC=3, K=4³=64, the K dim is tiny (192), so one program per `(B, output-spatial tile)` computing all 16 output channels in registers via a single GEMM tile is ideal. Fuse HardSwish into the conv epilogue so the conv output is never materialized.
- Better: fuse conv + HardSwish + the per-(B, group) reduction (sum and sumsq) into a single kernel — each program computes a tile of conv outputs, applies HardSwish, and atomically accumulates partial sums/sumsq into a small `(B, num_groups)` workspace; a second tiny kernel finalizes GN stats and writes `(B, C)`. This eliminates the full `(B, C, D, H, W)` write-then-read.
- Use channels-last memory ordering for the conv output tile so the per-channel reduction is contiguous, and exploit IC=3 by fully unrolling the input-channel loop as constexpr.
